emma: Quick question — we're planning to gate a new runtime feature (session-level KV cache prefetch + adaptive batching hint) behind different policies for hosted/dedicated/private. Want to align interfaces and auth boundaries before RFC. TL;DR: two proposals: 1) single unified API with capability negotiation, 2) explicit hosting-mode flags + adapter translation. Thoughts?

raj: I lean toward capability negotiation. Keeps client API stable and future-proof. But hosting differences (KMS/HSM, network isolation, volume mounts) mean some capabilities won't be available in some modes. We need clear semantics for 'unsupported' vs 'disabled'.

sasha: From runtime POV negotiation is doable. We can advertise per-connection capabilities like `kv_prefetch`, `adaptive_batching`, `stream_resume`. Question: do we make SDKs auto-fallback or require clients to ask for alternatives?

max: Concern: exposing capabilities encourages hacks that only work on hosted. Suggest server returns an `effective_capabilities` blob on first handshake and SDKs default to the intersection of portable features. Only explicit opt-in gets non-portable features.

emma: Also consider auth surfaces. Hosted uses Redwood tokens + KMS, Dedicated uses customer tokens + our sidecar, Private might use customer-managed KMS/HSM. Capability negotiation must not leak infra topology or secrets.

raj: Good point. We should treat capability flags as non-sensitive but avoid sending anything that indicates tenancy boundaries or key IDs. Runtime should map `requires_hsm` -> false for hosts w/o HSM, not reveal why.

sasha: Implementation sketch for handshake payload (proto-ish):
```json
{"handshake": {"client": "sdk-go-1.4", "wants": ["kv_prefetch","adaptive_batching"], "privacy": "opt-in"}}
```
Server reply:
```json
{"handshake": {"effective_capabilities": ["kv_prefetch"], "notes": "adaptive_batching unsupported: no hw-queue"}}
```
This keeps it explicit and machine-readable.

max: We also need a control-plane mapping so admin policies can override runtime-advertised capabilities (dedicated customer might opt out of kv_prefetch for cost reasons). Suggest a policy table: deployment -> capability -> fallback. Fallback example: `kv_prefetch` -> `prefix-kv-cache` or `none`; `adaptive_batching` -> `static-32`.

anna: One more constraint: private customers often forbid telemetry to leave their VPC. For private deployments, capability negotiation should be fully local and not hit our control plane unless customer admin opts in.

emma: Agreed. Add a `privacy` flag on the handshake: `privacy: local-only` will prevent recording capability telemetry. For hosted/dedicated default to `telemetry-allowed` unless customer sets otherwise.

infra-bot: Deploybot: added feature-gate `capability-negotiation` to canary env. config path: `/etc/redwood/feat/capneg=true`. CI pipeline will run handshake tests tonight. :rocket:

raj: Proposed next steps: 1) draft handshake proto + header (`X-Redwood-Effective-Capabilities`) RFC, 2) define control-plane policy mapping and admin UI, 3) runtime changes to compute and sanitize capability list, 4) SDK behavior: default to portable subset, explicit opt-in for non-portable, 5) privacy semantics for private deployments. I'll put a skeleton RFC up.

emma: Thanks. @sasha @max can you sketch runtime pseudo-code and a control-plane mapping example by EOD? I'll fold into the RFC and include privacy wording.

sasha: On it — will ping if I hit any blocker with KV isolation semantics.
__notes: thread about interface boundary choices for capability negotiation across hosted/dedicated/private. kept short, Slack style.
